articles.title: Modi at Delhi Dussehra: Unite, Defeat Enemies, Govern as Ram Rajya
articles.excerpt: At the Ravana Dahan in IP Extension on October 20, Prime Minister Narendra Modi defined India's enemies as forces that harm its honour, divide society and hate its culture, and held up Ram Rajya — no discrimination, equal justice and power as service — as the standard for governance and self-reliant development.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian Americans staging Ramlilas and Ravana Dahan at temples and community grounds for Vijayadashami, Modi's Delhi speech links the festival they celebrate abroad directly to debates at home over unity, cultural heritage and what good governance owes the poorest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Seeks All-Party Meeting After Manipur Civilian Killings
articles.excerpt: A delegation led by former Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh urged Chief Minister Khemchand Singh to convene all parties after three firewood collectors were killed in Imphal East; the Chief Minister assured them the demand would be looked into.
articles.nri_angle: Renewed violence and shutdowns in Manipur directly affect Manipuri families in the US and elsewhere who travel home and follow the state's security situation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Warns Gulf Situation Is Deep Concern in UAE Talks
articles.excerpt: Meeting UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai, Jaishankar backed dialogue, unimpeded energy and trade flows, and noted bilateral trade has crossed $100 billion since the CEPA.
articles.nri_angle: Jaishankar thanked the UAE leadership for ensuring the well-being of the large Indian community in the UAE, making diaspora welfare a formal item in the Mumbai talks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Early Flu Season and Mutated H1N1 Strain Raise Concern for Younger Americans
articles.excerpt: CDC data show flu positivity at 5.0% nationally and 10.7% on the West Coast, with H1N1 accounting for 96.4% of subtyped flu A viruses. Doctors recommend vaccination for everyone 6 months and older before the end of October.
articles.image_caption: An electron micrograph of the influenza virus. Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 is the dominant strain in CDC data this season.
articles.nri_angle: Multigenerational Indian American households with young children and older parents face the combined risk the data highlight, making October vaccination for every eligible family member the practical step.

articles.title: Celebrating Dussehra / Vijayadashami: A Festival of Victory and Goodness
articles.excerpt: Dussehra marks the triumph of good over evil in Indian culture.
articles.image_caption: Dussehra festival celebrations at Jakhu Temple. Dussehra (Vijayadashami) marks the victory of Rama over Ravana.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Rappers Turn Water Shortages and Heat Into a Climate Alarm
articles.excerpt: Kali, Abisha of Sollisai Sistahs and four other young artistes have released the six-track Climate Emergency Mixtape, billed as India's first multilingual rap album about the climate crisis.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh Represents India at SCO Heads of Government Meeting in Dushanbe
articles.excerpt: India's defence minister met Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref in Dushanbe, and used his SCO address to call for an end to double standards on terrorism.
articles.image_caption: India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh shakes hands with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda in front of an SCO backdrop in Dushanbe. Singh represented India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting on October 19-20, 2026.

articles.title: Supreme Court Orders Mandatory Insurance on All Railway Counter Tickets From October 27

articles.nri_angle: Millions of diaspora families travel by train in India, especially around Diwali; counter-bought tickets now carry the same accident cover as online bookings.

articles.title: Eight MGNREGA Workers Killed as Speeding Car Rams Roadside Crew in Sangrur

articles.excerpt: A rain-driven surge at the exit gate of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal on Saturday evening killed at least 17 people and injured 25, with later reports putting the toll at 19; police detained organisers and ordered a forensic probe.

articles.title: Unseasonal Rain Is Extending India's Dengue, Malaria and Flood-Disease Season
articles.excerpt: Rainfall above roughly 100 mm a month lifts dengue risk toward 2.3 times baseline, mosquitoes are colonising hill districts, and leptospirosis follows every flood.
articles.nri_angle: Families in India face a longer disease season after unseasonal rain; the precautions are concrete and household-level.

articles.title: India's 9.1% Pay Hikes Hide a Widening Split Over AI Skills, Aon Finds
articles.excerpt: Aon's survey of 1,200+ employers projects average hikes of 9.1% for 2027, but 37% of firms plan 10% or more while a quarter — including much of IT services — stay under 8% as AI-role premiums jump about 10%.
articles.image_caption: Bengaluru (file photo). Aon found India's 9.1% pay hikes mask a widening split over AI skills.

articles.title: FSSAI Proposes Ban on Added Sugars in Infant Food for Babies Under Six Months
articles.excerpt: A draft amendment published on October 16 would bar adding sucrose and fructose to products for infants up to six months, with 60 days for public comment before the rules can be finalised.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora parents who buy Indian-made infant food should note the ban is still a draft — sucrose and fructose remain permitted within limits until final rules are notified, so ingredient lists are the check that matters today.

articles.title: Delhi's AQI Leaps From 65 to 216 in a Day as Calm Weather Traps Pollution
articles.excerpt: Friday's rain briefly gave the capital satisfactory air. With the IMD forecasting dry, still days ahead, the winter pollution season has arrived early — and GRAP Stage 1 is already in force.
articles.image_caption: South Block is engulfed in a layer of smog in New Delhi. Delhi's AQI jumped from 65 to 216 in a day as dry, calm weather trapped pollutants over the capital.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families flying into Delhi for Diwali face AQI swings from 65 to 216 within a day; morning AQI checks and masks for sensitive travellers are now part of the trip.

articles.title: LK Advani, 98, Admitted to Delhi Hospital With Chest Infection, Condition Stable
articles.excerpt: The former deputy prime minister was brought to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Friday evening and is under observation in the pulmonary department. It is his third hospital admission in under two years.
articles.image_caption: L. K. Advani, the former deputy prime minister and BJP founding figure admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Delhi with a chest infection.
articles.nri_angle: Advani is a towering figure for a generation of Indians at home and abroad who followed the BJP's rise; his health is followed closely across the diaspora.

articles.title: Five Dead, Six Injured as Reactor Blast Rocks Bharuch Pharma Plant in Gujarat
articles.excerpt: A reactor failed during a hydrogenation process at a pharmaceutical unit in the Saykha GIDC area of Vagra, leaking methylene dichloride gas. Officials have opened an investigation and no cause has been established.
articles.image_caption: An injured person is loaded into an ambulance at night while medical staff and bystanders assist. The reactor blast at the Bharuch pharmaceutical plant killed five people and injured six, according to India Today.
articles.nri_angle: Bharuch's chemical belt is a major employer for Gujarati families in India and a region many in the diaspora come from; recurring fatal plant accidents there are a standing safety concern.

articles.title: 24 Indian Seafarers Safe After Tankers Hit in Hormuz and Off Romania, Minister Says
articles.excerpt: Crude tanker MT ST 3, with 15 Indian crew, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16; chemical tanker Yara J, with nine Indians aboard, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage on October 14. No casualties on either vessel.
articles.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's merchant crews; every attack on commercial shipping in the Gulf or Black Sea puts Indian families on shore on alert.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Asks UN Rights Office for Report on Pakistan's Actions in PoK
articles.excerpt: First Secretary Anuj Swarup pressed the OHCHR at the UN General Assembly for a follow-up on killings, detentions and internet restrictions in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, accusing it of extreme selectivity.
articles.image_caption: The Palais des Nations in Geneva, home of the UN Office at Geneva. India pressed the UN human rights office for a report on Pakistan's actions in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
articles.nri_angle: India's use of UN human rights forums on PoK is closely followed by the diaspora as part of the wider India-Pakistan contest at international institutions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Urges Urgent Multilateral Reform Through Stronger Minilateralism
articles.excerpt: At the Raisina Dialogue in Abu Dhabi, India's foreign minister cited a decade of India-UAE partnership as the model for smaller-group cooperation in a changing global order.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. Jaishankar urged urgent reform of multilateral institutions through stronger minilateralism at the Raisina Dialogue session in Abu Dhabi.
articles.nri_angle: The India-UAE partnership Jaishankar praised underpins trade, energy and consular protection for the roughly 4.3 million Indians living in the Emirates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement in force since May 2022

articles.title: Cabinet Clears 78-Day Diwali Bonus for 11.4 Lakh Railway Employees
articles.excerpt: The Rs 2,009.61 crore Productivity Linked Bonus pays up to Rs 17,951 per eligible employee — capped by a Rs 7,000 salary ceiling, dating to 2014-15, that unions want raised to Rs 18,000.
articles.nri_angle: The Rs 2,009.61 crore festival bonus reaches 11.4 lakh railway families — a workforce many diaspora households are part of — just as Diwali travel peaks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Starlink: Meet Security Rules, Build Local Base Stations First
articles.excerpt: New Delhi says Elon Musk's satellite internet service has not yet agreed to compliance conditions every operator must meet, as Bharti's Sunil Mittal argues his OneWeb venture is ahead in the approval queue.
articles.image_caption: A Starlink mission (file photo). India has told Starlink it must meet security rules and build local base stations before it can launch services in the country.
articles.nri_angle: Starlink's delayed India entry matters to diaspora families whose relatives in rural and remote parts of India still lack reliable broadband.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Himalayan Floods Test Whether India China Nepal Can Share Warnings
articles.excerpt: After the Aug. 26 flood killed 1,452 people in Nepal, Kathmandu is proposing a trilateral mechanism to share satellite data and early warnings across borders.
articles.nri_angle: Himalayan flood cooperation affects water security for hundreds of millions in the Ganga and Brahmaputra basins that diaspora families remain connected to.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Puducherry to Give Rs 700 Diwali Hampers to Three Lakh Ration Card Families
articles.excerpt: Each free hamper carries sugar, sunflower oil, chana dal, rava and maida, distributed through fair price shops before the festival, Minister V. P. Sivakolundhu announced in Karaikal.
articles.image_caption: Raj Nivas in Puducherry. The Union Territory government will give Rs 700 Diwali hampers to three lakh ration card families.
articles.nri_angle: Puducherry-origin families abroad can reassure ration-cardholder relatives at home: the hamper arrives automatically through their fair price shop, with no application needed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maharashtra Declares Drought in 305 Talukas, Promises Farmers Rs 5,000 Before Diwali
articles.excerpt: Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis added 40 talukas to the drought list, taking coverage past 85 percent of the state, and said the Rs 5,000 assistance will be credited before Diwali without waiting for central assessment.
articles.image_caption: Pandharpuri cattle at a government fodder camp in drought-affected Osmanabad district, Maharashtra (file photo). The state has declared drought in 305 talukas.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families remitting money to Maharashtra for Diwali can factor in the confirmed Rs 5,000 state payment due in farmers' accounts before the festival.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rashmika Mandanna Launches Project Annapurna, Adopting 400 Families for Grocery Support
articles.excerpt: The actor will cover grocery costs for 400 families at a time in three-month phases across eight South Indian locations, in an initiative she links to her Ranabaali character Jayamma.
articles.image_caption: Rashmika Mandanna. The actor launched Project Annapurna, adopting 400 families for grocery support.
articles.nri_angle: The phased, staples-first model offers diaspora readers a concrete template for funding food support for families back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Seeks Public Notice So All 51 War Victims' Families Can Claim Compensation
articles.excerpt: The court asked the External Affairs Ministry to consider a public notice inviting every bereaved family to claim, after the government said 51 Indians died, 139 were discharged and 77 remain untraced in the Russia-Ukraine war.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling matters to families across Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh — and to diaspora relatives helping them pursue claims, DNA identification and repatriation through the MEA.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meerut 'Blue Drum' Murder: Muskan and Sahil Sentenced to Death
articles.excerpt: A Meerut court handed down the death penalty after a 13-month trial built on circumstantial evidence, 126 hearings and 22 witnesses in the killing of merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput.
articles.nri_angle: The victim was a merchant navy officer who had just returned from London, a homecoming pattern familiar to many Indian seafarer and NRI families following the case from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Saurabh Rajput returns from London.
Rajput is sedated and murdered.
Body remains recovered from blue drum.
Muskan and Sahil convicted.

articles.title: Air India Frankfurt-Delhi Flight Diverted to Jaipur After Bomb Threat, Squawk 7500 Alert
articles.excerpt: Flight AI2030, a Boeing 787-9, made an emergency landing at Jaipur International Airport on Wednesday morning and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks. Air India's official comment was awaited.
articles.nri_angle: Frankfurt-Delhi is a core diaspora route between Germany and India; passengers on AI2030 faced an emergency diversion and security screening before any onward travel to Delhi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India, US Ironing Out Trade Deal Differences, Nearing a 'Landing Point': Jaishankar
articles.excerpt: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum that negotiators are working through the last differences on the bilateral trade pact, even as he stressed that the strategic partnership itself is unchanged.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. Jaishankar said India and the US are ironing out trade deal differences and nearing a landing point.
articles.nri_angle: A concluded trade deal would set the tariff terms Indian exporters and US-based Indian businesses trade under, after a year in which punitive US tariffs strained ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Boundary Has to Be Stable': Jaishankar Sets Condition for Normal China Ties
articles.excerpt: At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in Delhi, India's foreign minister tied normalisation with China to a quiet border, while keeping investment and market access as separate tracks.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. Jaishankar said normal ties with China require a stable border.
articles.nri_angle: India's China stance shapes trade, investment and security calculations followed closely across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio to Visit Mumbai and Jamnagar Oct. 17-22 for Energy, Strategic Talks
articles.excerpt: The US Secretary of State's second India visit this year pairs strategic-partnership talks with business meetings and a stop in Reliance's refining hub, with energy cooperation at the centre.
articles.image_caption: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar Oct. 17-22 for energy and strategic talks.
articles.nri_angle: A senior US visit focused on energy and investment, watched closely by Indian-American business and policy communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Jamnagar hosts the world's largest single-site refinery.
Refinery capacity: 1.4 million barrels of crude per day.
Rubio's visit follows increased US-India high-level contact.

items.event: Rubio arrives in Samarkand for C5+1 Ministerial.
Meetings with Central Asian officials.
Travel to Mumbai for business meetings.
Visit Jamnagar for energy discussions.
Departure from India.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal Invokes Ambedkar, Calls Opposition Street Protests the 'Grammar of Anarchy'
articles.excerpt: The commerce minister argues the courts are already handling the SIR and Form 6 dispute, so the Delhi marches demanding the election chief's dismissal have no constitutional excuse.
articles.image_caption: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal in a portrait from Wikimedia Commons. Goyal quoted B.R. Ambedkar on Tuesday to call Opposition street protests over voter-list revision the 'grammar of anarchy.'
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora following Indian politics, the fight is over how voter rolls are revised — a process that also governs NRI voter registration.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
